the cross-interval method is a simple, fast, and efficient method for detecting neural connectivity in neural networks.
the cross-interval method provides a simple, fast, and accurate method for determining connectivity in neural ensembes.
we have developed an on-line algorithm for estimating connectivity in neural networks that is robust and efficient and that is based on the timing of the spikes in the data.

methods for analyzing the interactions in neural ensembles and the presentation of a method which can greatly reduce the amount of time necessary for this analysis.
developing efficient techniques for the analysis of data from neural ensemles.
the development of a new technique for the analysis of neural data and the comparison of that technique to others.

the cross-interval technique performs well in a wide range of situations.
the cross-interval technique presented here is the best of the techniques presented here, and the only one that can be used on-line.
the method described here provides a fast and accurate means of determining the connectivity of a neural network, given that the number of neurons in the network is known.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an algorithm for detecting connections in a neural network.
the cross-interval technique is the most accurate, the timing technique is the fastest, and the bounded timing technique is a reasonable compromise.
the method presented here is the most efficient in the sense that it uses the least amount of data, and is the least restrictive, in the sense that the timing of the input can be unknown and bounded.

the cross-interval information method is the most computationally efficient method for estimating connectivity in neural ensemmbles.
